Single-trial N400 amplitudes

Source: R/data.R
n400.Rd

30 participants read German sentences ending in an expected or unexpected word (Er trinkt seinen Kaffee / Schrank). For each trial, the mean EEG amplitude 300-500 ms after the final word at nine electrodes. The N400 is more negative the less predictable the word (lower cloze probability), and largest over centro-parietal sites. 80 items, two counterbalanced lists.

Usage

n400

Format

A tibble with 21600 rows and 9 columns:

participant

Participant ID, P01 to P30.

list

Counterbalancing list, 1 or 2.

item

Item ID, i01 to i80.

condition

"expected" or "unexpected".

cloze

Cloze probability of the final word.

electrode

"F3", "Fz", "F4", "C3", "Cz", "C4", "P3", "Pz" or "P4".

anteriority

"frontal", "central" or "parietal".

laterality

"left", "midline" or "right".

amplitude

Mean amplitude in microvolts.

Source

data-raw/n400.R

Details

True model: amplitude = 2 + p0 + i0 + e0 + weight * (-4 + p1) * (1 - cloze) + trial + e. The electrode weight is 1 at Cz and Pz, 0.9 at the other central and parietal sites, 0.85 at Fz and 0.75 at F3 and F4; e0 is a small electrode offset. By-participant intercepts p0 (SD 1.5) and N400 slopes p1 (SD 1); by-item intercepts i0 (SD 0.5); trial noise shared across electrodes (SD 4) and electrode noise (SD 3). Cloze is 0.5 to 0.95 for expected and 0 to 0.05 for unexpected words. The midline weights follow the N400 difference waves in Kutas and Hillyard (1980, Experiment 2: -8.05, -9.62 and -9.24 microvolts at Fz, Cz and Pz); they recorded no lateral sites, so the lateral weights are simulated. In Kutas and Hillyard (1984), N400 amplitude tracked cloze probability closely at central and parietal sites (correlations of 0.90 to 0.92 for grand averages) and less at the frontal site (0.80). The sentences, participants and amplitudes here are simulated.

References

Kutas, M. & Hillyard, S. A. (1980). Reading senseless sentences: Brain potentials reflect semantic incongruity. Science, 207(4427), 203-205. doi:10.1126/science.7350657

Kutas, M. & Hillyard, S. A. (1984). Brain potentials during reading reflect word expectancy and semantic association. Nature, 307(5947), 161-163. doi:10.1038/307161a0

Examples

pz <- subset(n400, electrode == "Pz")
aggregate(amplitude ~ condition, data = pz, FUN = mean)
#>    condition amplitude
#> 1   expected  0.589250
#> 2 unexpected -2.103867
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  m <- lme4::lmer(amplitude ~ cloze + (1 + cloze | participant), data = pz)
  lme4::fixef(m)
}
#> (Intercept)       cloze 
#>    -2.15742     3.73584 
round(tapply(n400$amplitude, n400[c("anteriority", "condition")], mean), 2)
#>            condition
#> anteriority expected unexpected
#>    frontal      1.57      -0.71
#>    central      0.84      -1.87
#>    parietal     0.44      -2.07
